interpretation: Aristotle locates the good and the well in the work of those having a function, conditionally extends the analogy to humans if they have a function, and distinguishes the work of a lyre player from excellent lyre playing. This bounded reading evaluates exercises: good exercise qua role → excellent performance of its specified function. It does not assert that a skilled practitioner always performs well, infer a human function from the existence of crafts, or identify role-relative success with moral worth.
